title: Completing a task another active task depends on blocks all create/edit workspace-wide
description: Discovered 2026-09-04 as a direct side effect of completing QCLI-220 while QCLI-221 depended on it: canonicalizeTaskLinks (task create) and createTaskLinkSession/canonicalizeTaskLinks (task edit, edit-batch) were only ever shown snapshot.tasks -- the ACTIVE-only task set -- when resolving dependency and parentId edges. The moment any active task depends on (or is parented under) a task that gets completed or archived, that edge becomes unresolvable, and EVERY subsequent task create and task edit in the whole workspace fails with dependency_target_not_found, not just operations touching the two tasks involved. Verified directly against this repository live: quest task edit on a wholly unrelated task (QCLI-1, QCLI-2) failed identically once QCLI-220 completed while QCLI-221 depended on it. This is a P0 -- every fleet session using quest against this tracker was blocked from writing to it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: TaskService.create resolves dependency/parentId edges against every task location (tasks/completed/archive/tasks), not just active, while still reporting a specific task_already_exists (not a generic ambiguity) for a genuine id reuse against an existing record in any location
TaskService.editOn resolves the edited task's own dependency/parentId edges the same cross-location way, without changing which tasks are directly editable (still active-only via findTask)
TaskService.editBatch's graph-touching path (createTaskLinkSession) resolves against the same cross-location universe, not just the batch's active working set

The auto-allocated-id concurrent-create race (task_already_exists surfacing from a sibling writer's just-committed id) still maps to the existing retryable conflict envelope at the CLI layer, matching how dependency_target_ambiguous already did
A regression test proves: creating T2 depending on T1, completing T1, then creating/editing other tasks all still succeed (previously all failed)
bun run check passes in full (typecheck, lint, format, layers, all tests)

implementationNotes: Fleet exposure measured by opum-agent (orchestrator), 2026-09-04, checking the poisoning precondition across all five repos rather than assuming: relocated records (moved out of .quest/tasks/ by task complete/archive) -- opum-agent 25 tasks/0 relocated, opum-doc 135/0, opum-cli-e2e 26/0, lore-cli 427/1 (LCLI-429), quest-cli 218/4 (QCLI-217, 218, 220, 223). Of those, exactly one active-task edge points at a relocated task in the entire fleet: QCLI-221 (To Do) -> QCLI-220 (completed), the one created during this fix's own verification. lore-cli's relocated LCLI-429 has nothing depending on it, so it was unaffected despite having triggered the same relocation. Confirmed live (not just structurally) that opum-agent's own task edit still succeeds against the affected published 0.3.1 binary. The three zero-relocation repos are clean only because nobody there has ever run task complete -- all their terminal statuses were reached via task edit --status Done, which does not relocate (QCLI-221's open question). That makes this bug latently fleet-wide despite presently manifesting in one repository: the first task complete on a depended-upon task in any of the other four would trigger it. Correction for release notes: 0.3.2 fixes one write-locked workspace (quest-cli's own) and removes a trap the other four repos would hit on their next task complete -- it did not fix a live fleet-wide outage, since no other repo had actually hit it.
finalSummary: Fixed: create()/editOn()/editBatch() now resolve dependency/parentId edges against the full cross-location task set (this.taskRecords(snapshot)), not just active tasks, so a dependency on a completed/archived task no longer breaks every subsequent write. create() checks task_already_exists before canonicalization (not after) so explicit id reuse against a retired record reports the specific error, not a generic ambiguity; that error is now also mapped to the existing retryable conflict envelope at the CLI layer so the auto-id concurrent-create race still resolves the same way dependency_target_ambiguous always did. Verified live against this repo's own broken state (task edit on unrelated tasks failed identically before the fix, succeeded after), and via two new regression tests (cli-semantics.test.ts, cli-task-edit-batch.test.ts) confirmed to fail on the pre-fix code and pass on the fix. bun run check: 401/401 tests pass.
